title: Shoulder dislocation
overview: The humeral head loses its normal relationship with the glenoid.
mechanism: Anterior dislocation commonly follows forced abduction and external rotation.
findings: Pain, altered shoulder contour and restricted movement.
complications: Recurrent instability and injury to adjacent nerves or vessels.
limitation: Whole reference structures are highlighted; injury sites, tendon lesions, nerve geometry and pathological changes are not simulated.
objectives: Relate shoulder dislocation to the highlighted anatomy.
Explain the anatomical basis of typical findings and complications.

title: Rotator cuff tear
overview: A tear affects one or more tendons stabilizing the humeral head.
mechanism: Degeneration or an acute injury can disrupt the cuff.
findings: Shoulder pain and weakness with elevation or rotation.
complications: Persistent weakness and reduced shoulder function.
limitation: Whole reference structures are highlighted; injury sites, tendon lesions, nerve geometry and pathological changes are not simulated.

title: Proximal humeral fracture
overview: A fracture involves the upper end of the humerus.
mechanism: A fall or direct impact can injure the proximal humerus.
findings: Pain, swelling, bruising and difficulty moving the shoulder.
limitation: Whole reference structures are highlighted; injury sites, tendon lesions, nerve geometry and pathological changes are not simulated.

title: Humeral shaft fracture
overview: A fracture interrupts the shaft of the humerus.
mechanism: A fall, direct blow or twisting force can break the shaft.
findings: Arm pain, swelling and possible deformity.
complications: The radial nerve is vulnerable near the posterior humeral shaft.
limitation: Whole reference structures are highlighted; injury sites, tendon lesions, nerve geometry and pathological changes are not simulated.

title: Supracondylar fracture
overview: A fracture occurs above the distal humeral condyles, commonly in children.
mechanism: Often follows a fall onto an outstretched hand.
findings: Elbow pain, swelling and restricted movement.
complications: Brachial artery or nerve injury can threaten limb function.

title: Cubital tunnel syndrome
overview: The ulnar nerve is compressed around the elbow.
mechanism: Prolonged elbow flexion or local pressure may aggravate compression.
findings: Tingling in the little finger and ulnar half of the ring finger; grip may weaken.
complications: Longstanding compression can cause intrinsic hand muscle wasting.
limitation: Whole reference structures are highlighted; injury sites, tendon lesions, nerve geometry and pathological changes are not simulated.

title: Lateral epicondylitis
overview: A painful disorder of the common extensor tendon origin.
mechanism: Repetitive loading particularly involves extensor carpi radialis brevis.
findings: Lateral elbow tenderness and pain with gripping or resisted wrist extension.
complications: Persistent pain can limit work and activity.
limitation: Whole reference structures are highlighted; injury sites, tendon lesions, nerve geometry and pathological changes are not simulated.
objectives: Relate lateral epicondylitis to the highlighted anatomy.

title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
overview: The median nerve is compressed within the carpal tunnel.
mechanism: Increased pressure within the constrained tunnel affects the nerve.
findings: Numbness or tingling in the thumb, index, middle and radial ring finger; thenar weakness may develop.
complications: Persistent compression can produce sensory loss and thenar wasting.
limitation: Whole reference structures are highlighted; injury sites, tendon lesions, nerve geometry and pathological changes are not simulated.

title: Distal radius fracture
overview: A fracture involves the radius near the wrist.
mechanism: Often follows a fall onto an outstretched hand.
findings: Wrist pain, swelling and possible deformity.
complications: Stiffness and acute median nerve compression can occur.

title: Scaphoid fracture
overview: A fracture affects a carpal bone linking the two rows of the wrist.
mechanism: Often follows a fall onto an extended wrist.
findings: Radial wrist pain and tenderness near the anatomical snuffbox.
complications: Poor healing, nonunion and avascular necrosis are important concerns.

title: De Quervain tenosynovitis
overview: A painful tendon-sheath disorder affects abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis at the radial wrist.
mechanism: Tendon loading and sheath thickening restrict comfortable tendon movement.
findings: Radial wrist pain with thumb movement or grasping.
complications: Persistent pain can impair hand function.

title: Compartment syndrome
overview: Raised pressure in a muscle compartment impairs tissue perfusion.
mechanism: Bleeding or swelling after injury can raise pressure within closed fascia.
findings: Severe pain, swelling and pain on passive stretch are concerning features.
complications: Acute compartment syndrome is an emergency; muscle and nerve damage may become irreversible.
